serialFormats.description: 10-character Lennox serial (1973 to present): 2-digit plant/factory code, 2-digit year, 1 month letter (A-M skipping I), 5-digit production sequence. Used on residential and commercial equipment alike.
sources: Building Intelligence Center, 'Lennox HVAC age' (building-center.org/lennox-hvac-age/) - style 1 examples 1606B13871 (Feb 2006) and 5899L17212; positions 1-2 plant, 3-4 year, 5 month letter
PickHVAC, 'Lennox HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding' (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/lennox/) - month letters A-M skipping I; 5806E12345 = plant 58, May 2006
Parts Town, 'Lennox Serial Number Lookup' (partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/lennox-serial-number-lookup) - plant code list 51/53/54/55/56/58/63
hvacdecoder.com Lennox serial number decoder - agrees on plant/year/month-letter layout
notes: Year = characters 3-4 (two digits). Pivot 70: 73-99 -> 1973-1999, 00-69 -> 2000s. The format has been in continuous use since 1973 so a two-digit year is unambiguous within the era.
Month letter skips I: A=Jan ... H=Aug, J=Sep, K=Oct, L=Nov, M=Dec. A serial with I or N-Z in position 5 is not this format (re-read the plate).

Plant map covers only the codes documented by the secondary sources (51/53/54/55/56/58/63, confirmed by thedailythrive.org and furnace.direct / Parts Town; one lists 55 as 'Heatcraft', consistent with Stone Mountain, GA). Observed but unmapped plant codes: 16 (building-center example 1606B13871) and 52 (InspectorHandbook example 5207K24862 = Oct 2007) - the decoder reports the raw code. Unknown plant codes still decode (year/month).

Confidence is medium (three independent secondary decoders agree); Lennox's own 'Model and Serial Nomenclature' PDF (lennox.com/lib/legacy-res/pdfs/lennox_model_and_serial_nomenclature.pdf) is the primary source but could not be read in this session - promote to high once a warranty lookup on LennoxPros (Resources > Warranty lookup by serial) confirms three dated examples.
Residential and commercial Lennox units share this serial style; the difference is only the plant code (commercial rooftops are typically 56 Stuttgart AR or 58 Marshalltown IA).
Cross-check: the compressor date code and the refrigerant printed on the nameplate (R-22 before ~2008-2010 on rooftops, R-410A after, R-454B from 2025) should agree with the decoded year.

serialFormats.description: 9-character Lennox serial reported for the late 1970s to early 1990s: a letter, five digits, three letters; characters 2-3 are the year, the second-to-last character is the month letter.
sources: PickHVAC, 'Lennox HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding' (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/lennox/) - 'Style #2': letter + 5 numbers + 3 letters, 2nd/3rd characters = year (86 = 1986), second-to-last letter = month (D = April)
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: only one secondary source (PickHVAC) describes this style, and Building Intelligence Center states the 10-character plant/year/month style has been used exclusively since 1973 - the two sources disagree on whether this style exists. Treat any decode as a hint and confirm the year from the nameplate style and refrigerant (R-22 era).
The two examples are CONSTRUCTED to exercise the published rule; they are not real nameplates. Replace with dated nameplate photos when available.
The month-letter map (A-M skipping I) is assumed to match the 1973+ style; PickHVAC only confirms D = April.
No collision with the 10-character style: this style starts with a letter and is 9 characters long; the 1973+ style is all digits except position 5.

Only PickHVAC describes this style; Building Intelligence Center says the 10-character style has been exclusive since 1973 - when a serial matches both styles, prefer the 10-character decode. No second independent source was found in a verification pass of eight serial-related searches (a search-summary sample C89274AAC decodes to 1989-01 under this rule).

segments.name: Minor design sequence
segments.notes: 1 = 1st revision, 2 = 2nd, 3 = 3rd (per Raider ZCA nomenclature sheet; same Lennox convention).

segments.name: Voltage

notes: Nameplate: the factory model number is on the unit rating plate ('MODEL NO.') on the compressor/control-compartment side; it is the full string (e.g. LGH120H4BH1G) possibly followed by factory-option characters. LennoxPros catalog/stock numbers (L1318, 45W08 ...) are sales numbers, not model numbers - never decode those.
Service literature and engineering handbooks abbreviate the model (LGH120H4B, LGH036H4ES); the decoder accepts these partial strings.

Examples LGH120H4BH1G and LGH036H4ES1Y extend confirmed partial catalog strings (LGH120H4BH 460 V; LGH036H4ES 208-230 V 3 ph) with the minor-design digit and voltage letter; LCH150H4BN1G is constructed from the nomenclature. Verify against a real nameplate before relying on the last two positions.

controls.name: Lennox Prodigy (M2) / Prodigy 2.0 (M3) unit controller
controls.description: Microprocessor unit controller with LCD and push-button menu fitted to Energence (and late Strategos) rooftops: Prodigy M2 (2009-2013, setup guide 506215-01 / application guide 506457) and Prodigy 2.0 M3 (2013+, setup guide 507241-07, application guide 507242-07). faultCodes.meaning: Blower alarm (S52 blower airflow proving) - repeated code 5 alarms result in the 'STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER' lockout.

Dirty filters / closed dampers starving the blower

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 1 ROLLOUT OPEN S47 - Heat section 1 locked out after repeated roll-out switch opens. Check roll out sensor and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Repeated rollout trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 54, reset S47, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 54-55; parallel entry 65 'STRIKE 3 ROLLOUT OPEN S69')
faultCodes.notes: Display wording reconstructed from the documented row pattern, not seen verbatim in a Table 65 excerpt - verify against Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 pp.153-156 / 507242-07). Label inferred from the heat-2 pair 64/65; verify exact wording.

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 1 CAI SWITCH S18 - Check heat section 1 combustion air motor and proof switch. Set if S18 is not sensed closed within 30 seconds of energizing the combustion air inducer (closed-proof alarm).
likelyCauses: Combustion air inducer not running or weak (motor, capacitor, wiring)
Blocked flue / inlet, cracked or plugged pressure-switch tubing
Failed S18 proof switch
checks: Confirm the inducer runs on a heat call and check its amps
Check S18 tubing and switch make/break
Check flue and combustion air inlet for obstruction
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 56-57) and 'Combustion Air Inducer Proof Switch (S18 and S45)' section (ManualsLib 1593305 p.18)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 1 CAI SWITCH S18 - Heat section 1 locked out after three CAI proof-switch failures during a single demand. Check heat section 1 combustion air motor and proof switch.
likelyCauses: Repeated S18 proving failures
checks: Fix the cause of code 56, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1593305 p.139 'ALARM STRIKE 3 HEAT 1 CAI SWITCH S18') and CAI section ('alarm(s) 57 and/or 67 when three-strikes occur during a single-demand')

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 1 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV1 - The M3 unit controller did not detect that the gas valve was energized within two minutes after a heating demand. Check ignition control, flame proof, GV1, gas supply.
likelyCauses: Ignition control A3 lockout (no flame / no spark)
Gas supply off or low pressure
Gas valve or its sensing feedback wiring open
checks: Watch the ignition control's status LED during a heat call
Verify gas supply and manifold pressure
Check GV1 feedback wiring to the M3
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 58-59) and 'Gas Valve Sensing' text ('error code 58 for gas heat section 1 and alarm 68 for gas heat section 2')

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV1 - Gas valve was energized and de-energized three times (default) during a single heating demand; heat section 1 locked out. Check ignition control, flame proof, GV1, gas supply.
likelyCauses: Flame loss / flame-sense problems (dirty flame rod, poor ground, low gas pressure)
Intermittent ignition control
checks: Check flame signal, flame rod and burner ground
Check gas pressure under load
Clear the lockout via the Service menu after repair
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 and 'Gas Valve Sensing' text ('error code 59 for the gas heat section 1')

faultCodes.meaning: PRIMARY HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S99 - Heat section 2 primary gas heat limit switch is open. Check air flow, air filter, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Low airflow, over-firing, or failed S99 limit on heat section 2
checks: As for code 50, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (code 61 'STRIKE 3 PRIMARY HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S99' implies 60 is the first-strike entry) and 'Primary or Secondary Limits (S10 and S99)' section
faultCodes.notes: The guide's gas-valve-sensing narrative also cites 'alarm 60 for gas heat section 2' for a cycled gas valve; Table 65 lists that condition as 69. Treat 60 as the heat 2 primary limit and verify against the table.

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 PRIMARY HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S99 - Check heat section 2 primary burner limit switch to see if it is open. Check air flow, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Repeated S99 trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 60, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S100 - Heat section 2 secondary heat limit switch is open. Check air flow, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Low airflow, over-firing, or failed S100 secondary limit
checks: As for code 52, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 2 LIMIT OPEN S100 - Heat section 2 secondary heat limit switch is open (three strikes). Check air flow, limit switch and wiring.
likelyCauses: Repeated S100 trips
checks: Fix the cause of code 62, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 ROLLOUT OPEN S69 - Check roll out sensor and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Flame rollout on heat section 2 (blocked flue/heat exchanger, combustion air)
Tripped manual-reset rollout switch S69
checks: Find the cause before resetting S69; inspect heat exchanger, flue and burners
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 ROLLOUT OPEN S69 - Check roll out sensor and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Repeated rollout trips on heat section 2
checks: Fix the cause of code 64, reset S69, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 CAI SWITCH S45 - Check heat section 2 combustion air motor and proof switch. Set if S45 is not sensed closed within 30 seconds of energizing the combustion air inducer.
likelyCauses: Inducer 2 not running, blocked flue/inlet, tubing, or failed S45
checks: As for code 56, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 and CAI proof switch section ('Alarm 56 or 66')

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 HEAT 2 CAI SWITCH S45 - Heat section 2 locked out after three CAI proof-switch failures in a single demand.
likelyCauses: Repeated S45 proving failures
checks: Fix the cause of code 66, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 and CAI section ('alarm(s) 57 and/or 67')

faultCodes.meaning: HEAT 2 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV3 - Gas valve for heat section 2 not detected energized within two minutes after a heating demand. Check heat section 2 ignition control, flame proof, gas valve and gas supply.
likelyCauses: Ignition control lockout on heat section 2, gas supply, or valve feedback wiring
checks: As for code 58, on heat section 2
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (codes 68-69) and 'Gas Valve Sensing' text ('alarm 68 for gas heat section 2')
faultCodes.notes: Heat section 2 valve is designated GV3 in Table 65 (codes 45 and 69); one summary labelled 68 as GV2.

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 NO PROOF GAS VALVE GV3 HEAT SECT 2 - Check ignition control, flame proof, GV3, gas supply.
likelyCauses: Repeated flame loss / gas valve cycling on heat section 2
checks: Fix the cause of code 68, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: NETWORK SENSOR ERROR - Check with integrator for refresh rate, network status lights and wiring. Alarm is removed when all BACnet network sensor inputs are received.
likelyCauses: BAS not writing a required network sensor value (zone temp, setpoint, etc.) within the refresh time
BACnet/LonTalk module or network wiring problem
checks: Confirm the BAS is writing every network sensor the configuration expects
Check module TX/RX LEDs and network wiring/termination
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150); M3 BACnet Module guide 1404

faultCodes.meaning: NO ZONE SENSOR - No zone sensor input; check zone sensor and wiring. (Backup sensor mode / code 93 follows if configured.)
likelyCauses: Unit configured for zone-sensor mode but wired for a thermostat
Open/shorted zone sensor A2 or its wiring
checks: Determine whether the unit should be in zone sensor or thermostat mode; setting it back to thermostat mode clears 74 and 93
Check A2 zone sensor resistance and wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65; Lennox Commercial Controls FAQ 507398 (codes 74/93)

faultCodes.meaning: OUTDOOR TEMP SENSOR RT17 - Check sensor and wiring.
likelyCauses: Open or shorted RT17 outdoor air thermistor or wiring
checks: Measure RT17 resistance vs temperature (two-wire thermistor); check wiring and plug
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: HUMIDITY SENSOR A91 - Check 2 amp fuse and sensor/wiring.
likelyCauses: Blown 2 A fuse feeding the sensor
Open/shorted humidity sensor A91 or wiring; sensor not installed but enabled
checks: Check the 2 amp fuse
Check A91 supply voltage and signal; verify the humidity-sensor configuration if no sensor is fitted
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: DISCHARGE AIR TEMP SENSOR RT6 - Check sensor and wiring.
likelyCauses: Open or shorted RT6 discharge air thermistor (located in the discharge air just beyond the heat exchanger, accessible through the blower compartment)
checks: Measure RT6 resistance and check wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: RETURN AIR TEMP SENSOR RT16 - Check sensor and wiring.
likelyCauses: Open or shorted RT16 return air thermistor or wiring
checks: Measure RT16 resistance and check wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: ADD-ON BOARD PROBLEM - Check add-on board and reset to clear.
likelyCauses: Add-on controller (e.g. C1/ECTO expansion, GP board) not communicating or failed
checks: Check add-on board connections and power; reset the controller to clear
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.150)

faultCodes.meaning: REHEAT SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: Humiditrol / supermarket reheat option configured without the required hardware or settings
checks: Review reheat (Humiditrol) settings in the unit configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: CONTROLLER RESET
likelyCauses: Controller restarted (power interruption, firmware watchdog)
checks: Check power quality; note frequency of resets in alarm history
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: INCORRECT SETTINGS
likelyCauses: Conflicting unit configuration ID / parameter settings
checks: Re-check the unit configuration ID against the nameplate and the setup guide
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: INCORRECT HUMIDITROL SETTINGS
likelyCauses: Humiditrol dehumidification configured inconsistently with the installed hardware
checks: Review the Humiditrol settings and dehumidification mode configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: CONFLICTING THERMOSTAT INPUT
likelyCauses: Simultaneous heating and cooling (Y and W) demands, or stage inputs present without the first stage
Thermostat wiring or thermostat fault
checks: Check thermostat inputs at the M3 (Y1/Y2/W1/W2/G) with a meter
Verify thermostat wiring and staging
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.151)

faultCodes.meaning: BACKUP SENSOR MODE - Communication with the zone sensor was lost and the unit switched to the redundant back-up sensor (code broadcast over BACnet and shown on the Prodigy display). Check zone sensor and wiring; usually accompanies code 74.
likelyCauses: Zone sensor failure or wiring (see code 74)
Unit left in zone-sensor mode on a thermostat installation
checks: Fix the code 74 cause; change the unit back to thermostat mode if a thermostat is used
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65; Lennox Commercial Controls FAQ 507398; M3 BACnet Module guide 1404

faultCodes.meaning: MGV CONTROL SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: Modulating gas valve control option configured without the required settings/hardware
checks: Review the modulating gas heat configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: GP CONTROL SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: General-purpose (GP) control add-on configured inconsistently
checks: Review GP board configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED CONTROL SETUP ERROR
likelyCauses: Advanced control option settings conflict
checks: Review advanced control settings in the configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: BUILDING PRESSURE SENSOR A34
likelyCauses: Building pressure sensor A34 signal out of range, missing, or wiring open
checks: Check A34 power, signal and tubing; verify the building pressure control option matches installed hardware
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: SUPPLY STATIC PRESSURE SENSOR ERROR (A30) - The Prodigy controller locks out unit operation after the Max Static Duct Pressure Occurrences have occurred.
likelyCauses: Duct static sensor A30 signal out of range, tubing disconnected, or wiring fault
checks: Check A30 supply voltage, output signal and sensing tubing
Verify the MSAV / VAV static-pressure configuration
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: HIGH SUPPLY STATIC (DUCT) PRESSURE - Unit operation locked out after the Max Static Duct Pressure Occurrences.
likelyCauses: Closed VAV boxes / dampers, blocked ductwork, high-limit static setpoint too low
VFD not responding to the static-pressure control
checks: Check duct static against the high-limit setpoint; check VAV box operation and VFD control
Clear the lockout via the Service menu after correcting
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: STRIKE 3 DUCT SUPPLY PRESS SENSOR A30
likelyCauses: Repeated supply static sensor errors
checks: Fix the cause of code 107, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: WAITING ON NETWORK DATA
likelyCauses: Unit configured for network (BAS) control and required network values have not yet been received
checks: Confirm the BAS is writing the required points; check network wiring and module LEDs
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: PROFILE ERROR
likelyCauses: Unit profile / configuration data invalid
checks: Reload or verify the unit configuration; contact Lennox technical support if it persists
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.152)

faultCodes.meaning: ADD-ON BOARD MCB PROBLEM
likelyCauses: Add-on control board communication or hardware fault
checks: Check add-on board connections; reset the controller
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: LINE FREQ DOES NOT MATCH UNIT CONFIG
likelyCauses: 50/60 Hz configuration does not match the measured line frequency
Poor power quality (generator) confusing the phase/voltage detection
checks: Verify the unit configuration frequency setting against the supply
Check power source quality
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC PRIMARY VOLTAGE LOW - Set when the calculated RMS 24 VAC is below the low-voltage alarm threshold (30 VAC per the guide's low-voltage text) for more than two seconds; the controller stops cooling, heating and ventilation.
likelyCauses: Low line voltage or wrong transformer primary tap
Overloaded / failing control transformer T1
High-resistance connections on the 24 VAC circuit
checks: Measure T1 secondary under load and line voltage at the unit
Check transformer tap selection for the supply voltage
Check 24 VAC wiring and connections
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155) and 'Phase-Voltage Detection' section (p.147)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC PRIMARY VOLTAGE HIGH - Calculated RMS 24 VAC above the high-voltage alarm threshold for more than two seconds.
likelyCauses: High line voltage or wrong transformer tap
checks: Measure T1 output and line voltage; correct the tap
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC SECONDARY VOLTAGE LOW
likelyCauses: Low secondary 24 VAC supply (second transformer/circuit) - overload, loose connection, transformer failing
checks: Measure the secondary 24 VAC circuit under load; check connections
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC SECONDARY VOLTAGE HIGH
likelyCauses: High secondary 24 VAC supply (line voltage / tap)
checks: Measure the secondary 24 VAC circuit; correct transformer tap
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: LINE PHASING DOES NOT MATCH UNIT CONFIG
likelyCauses: Phase rotation reversed (scroll compressors run backwards)
Single-phase/three-phase setting wrong in the configuration; DI-2 misconfigured when phase/voltage detection is enabled (unit goes to demand hold and restarts after 3 minutes)
checks: Check phase rotation with a meter and swap two incoming legs if reversed
Verify Config ID 2 position 5 (phase/voltage detection) and DI-2 settings
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155) and 'Phase-Voltage Detection' section

faultCodes.meaning: 24VAC POWER LOSS
likelyCauses: Interruption of 24 VAC control power (transformer, fuse, disconnect, erratic supply)
checks: Check the control transformer, 2 A fuse and incoming power connections
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: VFD SHUTDOWN - VFD fault detected. Check belt and for blower overload. Fix source of fault and reset.
likelyCauses: VFD tripped (overcurrent, overload, DC bus, overtemperature)
Seized blower bearing, belt, or motor fault
checks: Read the fault code on the VFD keypad
Check belt, bearings and motor amps; reset the VFD after repair
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: VFD BYPASS ENGAGED - VFD bypass mode is engaged. Blower may or may not be on. Disengage at MSAV menu.
likelyCauses: Bypass selected in the MSAV (VFD) menu, or bypass contactor engaged
checks: Disengage bypass from the MSAV menu once the VFD is repaired
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW OUTSIDE AIR DAMPER/ECON MECHANICAL FAULT - Damper feedback voltage not within +/- 0.15 V (+/- 2%) of the target within the predefined time.
likelyCauses: Damper actuator failed, binding linkage, or feedback wiring open
Damper blades obstructed / seized
checks: Command the damper in Service > Test and watch the 2-10 V feedback
Check actuator power, control and feedback wiring, and linkage
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Damper Diagnostics' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65
faultCodes.notes: 'Advanced Airflow' on the user interface means Smart Airflow.

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW LOW OUTDOOR AIRFLOW - Actual outdoor air less than target by the percentage set by parameter 239 (default 25%) for the time set by parameter 243 (default 1800 s).
likelyCauses: Blocked outdoor air hood / filters, damper not opening fully
Damper pressure sensor PT5 or supply CFM measurement error
checks: Check outdoor-air hood, filters and damper travel
Check PT5 tubing and sensor
Review parameters 239 and 243
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Ventilation Errors' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW OUTDOOR AIRFLOW TOO HIGH - Actual outdoor air greater than target by the percentage set by parameter 240 for the duration set by parameter 244.
likelyCauses: Damper stuck open or over-travelling; leaking damper blades
PT5 measurement error
checks: Check damper closing and blade seals
Check PT5 tubing/sensor; review parameters 240 and 244
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Ventilation Errors' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: ADVANCED AIRFLOW DAMPER PRESSURE ERROR - Differential pressure across the damper (PT5) found not legitimate for the period set by parameter 245.
likelyCauses: PT5 pressure transducer or tubing fault (disconnected, kinked, wrong ports)
Damper position feedback inconsistent with measured pressure
checks: Check PT5 tubing to both sides of the damper and the transducer output
Verify damper feedback and blade condition
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Damper Diagnostics' (ManualsLib 1251298 p.82) and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: CAI PRESSURE SWITCH STUCK CLOSED - GV1 - Set if S18 is not proved open while the combustion air blower is not energized (open-proof check).
likelyCauses: Proof switch S18 contacts welded / stuck closed
Switch wiring shorted
Inducer still spinning or draft holding the switch closed
checks: With the inducer off, verify S18 contacts are open
Replace S18 if stuck; check wiring for shorts
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Combustion Air Inducer Proof Switch (S18 and S45)' (ManualsLib 1593305 p.18) and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: CAI PRESSURE SWITCH STUCK CLOSED - GV2 - Set if S45 is not proved open while the combustion air blower is not energized.
likelyCauses: Proof switch S45 stuck closed or wiring shorted
checks: As for code 166, on heat section 2 (S45)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 CAI proof switch section and Table 65
faultCodes.notes: Table labels this GV2 although heat section 2 alarms elsewhere use GV3; label is as displayed.

faultCodes.meaning: COMBUSTION AIR SW NOT OPEN LOCKOUT - GV1 - Set (instead of 166) when S18 is not proved open, with the combustion air blower not energized, 5 consecutive times during a single cycle.
likelyCauses: Repeated stuck-closed S18
checks: Replace/repair S18, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 CAI proof switch section and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: COMBUSTION AIR SW NOT OPEN LOCKOUT - GV2 - Set (instead of 167) when S45 is not proved open 5 consecutive times during a single cycle.
likelyCauses: Repeated stuck-closed S45
checks: Replace/repair S45, then clear the lockout via the Service menu
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 CAI proof switch section and Table 65

faultCodes.meaning: ULTRA: COMPRESSOR 1 SUMP TEMPERATURE SENSOR ERROR
likelyCauses: Compressor 1 sump (crankcase) temperature sensor open/shorted or wiring fault (Energence Ultra-High Efficiency variable-speed units)
checks: Check the sump sensor resistance and wiring at the inverter/M3
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: ULTRA: COMPRESSOR 2 SUMP TEMPERATURE SENSOR ERROR
likelyCauses: Compressor 2 sump temperature sensor open/shorted or wiring fault
checks: Check the sump sensor resistance and wiring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: ENGINEERING USE ONLY
likelyCauses: Internal/engineering diagnostic event
checks: No field action defined; note in alarm history and contact Lennox if recurring
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: BLOWER MOTOR FAULT
likelyCauses: Blower motor / motor controller reporting a fault (overload, overtemperature, communication)
checks: Check blower motor amps, bearings, belt and the motor controller/VFD fault log
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: INVERTER LOW LEVEL ALARM
likelyCauses: Compressor inverter reporting a non-lockout (low-level) warning
checks: Read the inverter's own status/error code; check inverter power, cooling and communications
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155)

faultCodes.meaning: INVERTER ERROR - The alarming value is the inverter error code (e.g. 21 = Peak DC current, 22 = Maximum current reached lockout, 23 = DC Link low voltage). Alarm clears automatically when the inverter error clears.
likelyCauses: Inverter overcurrent / DC bus problems from power quality, compressor mechanical load, or inverter hardware
Loose power wiring to the inverter
checks: Record the alarming value and look it up in the inverter error list in the application guide
Check incoming voltage/phase balance and inverter power connections
Check compressor windings and mechanical condition if current-related
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.155-156)

faultCodes.meaning: INVERTER COMMUNICATION - Unable to communicate with inverter. Prodigy will disable compressor operation. Replace communication cable between inverter and M3 unit controller; if alarm continues, replace M3 unit controller or inverter.
likelyCauses: Damaged or unplugged inverter-to-M3 communication cable
Inverter unpowered or failed; M3 comm port failure
checks: Check the inverter has power and its status LEDs
Reseat/replace the communication cable
Replace M3 or inverter if communication does not return
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (ManualsLib 1251298 p.156)
faultCodes.notes: Two search summaries of the same page cited this row as 189 and as 190; verify the code number in Table 65.

faultCodes.meaning: ERRATIC POWER - Erratic Power - Set whenever service is turned off due to detection of power loss (loss-of-power detection, single-phase units). Check power connections. User can clear the alarm via the user interface.
likelyCauses: Loose or corroded power connections, failing disconnect or contactor
Utility power interruptions / brownouts
checks: Check incoming power connections and voltage stability
Clear the alarm from the user interface after correcting
faultCodes.source: Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 'Loss of Power Detection (Single-Phase Units Only)' (ManualsLib 1593305 p.17) and Table 65
faultCodes.notes: Alarm number 1 per the M-series numbering (CORE Table 11 'Erratic Power (Alarm 1)'; IMC code 1 'Power loss for two cycles'); the related M3 numeric alarm for a full loss of control power is 128 '24VAC POWER LOSS'.

faultCodes.meaning: CONTROLLER PROBLEM - INTERNAL CONTROLLER PROBLEM (Prodigy M2 only).
likelyCauses: Internal M2 controller hardware/firmware fault
checks: Reset the controller; if it persists replace the M2 (kit 102630-01)
faultCodes.source: Prodigy M2 Installation & Setup Guide 506215-01 Table 8 Alarm Codes
faultCodes.notes: Not seen in a search excerpt of the Prodigy M2 guide 506215-01 (neuco IS-59W47) this session; keep as low-confidence until confirmed in its Table 8. On the Prodigy 2.0 M3, codes 112-119 are reserved.

faultCodes.meaning: CONTROLLER PROBLEM - POWER NOISE PROBLEM (Prodigy M2 only). See Service Flash CU-10-2 for an in-depth look at error 114.
likelyCauses: Electrical noise on the 24 VAC / ground (poor grounding, shared transformer, VFD noise)
checks: Check unit and controller grounding and transformer wiring per Service Flash CU-10-2
Isolate noisy loads from the control transformer
faultCodes.source: Prodigy M2 Installation & Setup Guide 506215-01 Table 8; Lennox Service Flash CU-10-2

diagnosticTips: Alarms and events are listed in the Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65/66 (Alarm and Event Codes); alarms marked with * close the service relay DO1. Prodigy (M2) uses Application Guide 506457.

Lockouts ('STRIKE 3 ...' alarms) are cleared from the Service menu (Service > Lockouts / clear lockouts) after the fault is corrected; the number of strikes defaults to 3 (parameter 43 for blower; parameter 98 for high pressure/high temp, 99 for low pressure, 81 for freeze-stat). Even if an alternate occurrence count is set, the alarm text still says 'STRIKE 3'.
Use the LennoxPros 'Error Code Lookup' tool (Technical Tools on LennoxPros.com or the LennoxPros app) to look up any Prodigy alarm number with troubleshooting steps.
Lennox Commercial Technical Support: 800-453-6669 (800-4-LENNOX), 9am-6pm CT; National Accounts 800-367-6285, 8am-5pm CT (lennox.com/commercial/connect).

The M3 has an LCD with menu buttons on the controller face (unit control box). Active alarms take over the screen; press BACK to dismiss the full-screen alarm - the condition still exists and up to two alarm codes stay displayed along the right side of the screen above the thermostat-demand status.

Alarm history: error codes are stored and can be recalled later from the Alarms menu (Settings/Service); the Prodigy M2 Installation & Setup Guide covers viewing and silencing alarms via the user interface.

Test mode: SERVICE > TEST lets you run individual outputs (blower, compressors, heat, damper, exhaust); press SELECT to disable the active test when done. The heartbeat LED is steady green while in test/configuration mode.
Alarms marked with * in Table 65 close the service relay output DO1 (service alarm output) when configured.

Phase/voltage detection (Config ID 2, position 5): N = not installed, 1 = internal Lennox detection, 2/3 = external A42 phase monitor on DI-2 / DI-3. Wrong DI-2 configuration with detection enabled on three-phase units causes demand hold and a 3-minute restart.

Coverage note: Table 65 rows not yet captured: 3, 7, 9-11, 21, 31, 46-49, 80, 87-92, 94-100, 131-135, 138, 140-142, 144-165, 170-177, 186, 190+ (reserved on the M3: 70-72, 84, 104-105, 112-119, 127, 178-181). Rows 17, 18, 19, 54 and 55 have display text reconstructed from the row pattern (evidence single_secondary); rows 40 and 60 were confirmed. The guide states events 12-19 are the high-pressure/high-temperature events.

controls.name: Lennox CORE Control System (M4 unit controller) and CORE Lite
controls.description: Current Lennox unit controller (M4) on Model L (LGM/LCM), Enlight, late Energence and other rooftops, with a four-character seven-segment LED on the board, an optional display and the CORE Service App; CORE Lite is the reduced version on Xion. Numeric alarm codes with a display message and an event action (cause + solution) are listed in the CORE Application Guide 485115 Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' (also Setup Guide 508111-01 p.37+). Coverage is partial. Codes with evidence 'manufacturer_doc' were seen in a CORE (M4) document excerpt; codes with 'single_secondary'/'multi_secondary' were copied from the Prodigy 2.0 (M3) Table 65 transcription, which uses the same alarm numbering CORE inherits (spot-checked identical for 1, 4, 5, 13-15, 22-23, 42-43, 82-83, 85) - verify those against Table 11 before relying on them. Alarms captured by message but not by number (ADD ON BOARD PROBLEM, OAC ERROR, No 24VAC relay power A61/TB34-1, RT6/RT17 sensor alarms) are entered with the display text as the code. Expected by pattern but unconfirmed: 16/17 (S28 comp 3), 18/19 (S96 comp 4; 'HIGH PRESS S96 OPEN COMP4' seen without its number), 25, 26-29, 30-37, 45-56 and 121-126. CORE Lite (508676-01) uses the same numbering for the functions it supports.

diagnosticTips: Alarm codes are shown on the CORE display with a message and an event action; the full list with cause/solution is Table 11 of the CORE Application Guide 485115 (and the CORE Lite guide 508676-01). Model L specifics are in the CORE Information Guide 508111-03.
Initial configuration, test/service modes and network setup are in the CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01.

Local interface: the M4 CORE board has a four-character seven-segment LED that shows status codes by display priority (see ledPatterns, from the CORE Application Guide 485115 'Local Interface - Four Character Seven-Segment LED' table) and active alarm numbers; full alarm text, time of occurrence and troubleshooting text are shown in the CORE Service App (Bluetooth mobile app, 'Alarms' section) and on the optional display. Alarm history and logs can also be pulled through the USB port.

Alarm numbers, display messages and event actions (cause + solution) are Table 11 'CORE Control System Alarm and Event Codes' in the CORE Unit Controller Setup Guide 508111-01 (page 37 onward) and section 26.3 of the Application Guide 485115; the CORE Lite equivalent is section 19.3 of guide 508676-01.

Alarms marked * in Table 11 close the service relay contacts (DO1). The contacts stay closed until the controller resets, or the alarm condition clears and the alarm status is read via an explicit S-BUS command.

Compressor strike-3 lockouts (high pressure, low pressure, freezestat) are cleared from the Service menu after correcting the fault. Alarm 83 INCORRECT SETTINGS clears only by resetting or power-cycling the controller.

High-pressure alarms clear when the switch is detected closed; the compressor will not restart until the switch is closed and the Minimum Off Delay has expired. Low-pressure switches are shunted/ignored for 120 s (default, 0-600 s) after a demand; three trips within a demand lock the stage out.
Freezestats S49/S50/S53/S95 (compressors 1-4) are auto-reset: open at 29 F +/-3 on a fall, close at 58 F +/-4 on a rise; three openings lock the compressor out.
Air-flow proving switch S52 must close within 16 s of blower start or alarm 5 shuts the unit down; dirty-filter switch S27 only logs an alarm and can drive the service relay.

Phase/voltage detection: alarms 122-125 are auto-resetting and operation is restored five minutes after proper voltage returns; alarms 121 and 126 require removing power and correcting the problem before service is restored.
Economizer damper diagnostics use the actuator feedback voltage at P262 (DPOS, 2-10 V = 0-100 %); a feedback mismatch of more than +/-0.15 V after the allowed travel time raises alarm 136.
The LennoxPros Error Code Lookup tool (LennoxPros.com) covers CORE/M4 alarm numbers with troubleshooting steps.

controls.description: Board-mounted microprocessor controller (A55, versions M1-4 through M1-8) on L Series and S-Class (Strategos) gas/electric, electric/electric and heat pump rooftops (c. 1997-2012). Error codes are shown on a 3-digit LED readout on the A55 board (it shows 8.8.8 at power-up) and stored for recall through the pushbutton and MODE DIP switches; configured by DIP switches and ECTO parameters; optional IMC BACnet module and L Connection network. Codes 1-127 were transcribed from the M1-7 Version 5.02 manual Table 4 'IMC Error Codes' via search-engine excerpts of the manualzz text index and the lennoxeurope PDF; the M1-8 Version 6 door label uses the same numbering (codes 1-127). Coverage is partial only because codes 103 and 105 could not be captured cleanly (search excerpts conflated them with 104 and 107) and the gap numbers 7-9, 30-31, 42-43, 70-72 and 111-126 (believed reserved) were not seen verbatim, so they are not listed.

diagnosticTips: Error codes are shown on the A55 IMC board's 3-digit LED readout and stored for later recall (IMC manual Table 4 and Figure 16 list every code; M1-7 v5.02 is at webmanuals.lennoxeurope.com / manualzz 'IMC V7').
The IMC shunts the low-pressure switches (S87/S88) during compressor start until pressure stabilizes, so a low-pressure trip logged after the delay is a real refrigerant/airflow problem.

Where to look: the A55 (M1-7/M1-8) board in the unit control box carries a multi-digit LED readout, a single pushbutton, a green heartbeat LED and MODE DIP switches (UNIT TEST, RECALL, ECTO, TEMP, OPT2, SHIFT). Active error codes are shown on the readout; every code is also stored for recall.

Read stored codes: set the MODE DIP RECALL switch ON, then short-push the pushbutton; stored codes display in reverse order (most recent first) with each short push. A zero means nothing is stored. Set RECALL back OFF when done.
Clear stored codes: with RECALL ON, hold the pushbutton down until 0 is displayed, then turn RECALL OFF.

Reset a lockout: two successive short pushes of the pushbutton reset counters, lockout conditions and timers (codes marked "locked off/locked out" - 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 33, 35, 37, 39, 51, 53, 55, 57, 59, 61, 63, 65, 67, 69, 109). A control power reset does the same. Fix the root cause first; manual-reset rollout switches (S47/S69) must be reset at the switch.
A single push of the pushbutton advances to the next display; a double push returns to the previous display (used in ECTO/TEMP modes).

Unit test: the UNIT TEST DIP switch / "Testing Unit Function" section lets the IMC drive individual outputs (blower, compressors, fans, reversing valve, service relay) to check components; thermostat demands can also be simulated by jumpering TB1-6 to TB1-3 (blower), TB1-18 (Y1), TB1-12 (Y2) or TB1-2 (W1). A short push of the pushbutton skips the current delay timer.
The service output (24 VAC alarm relay) is energized by default on the lockout errors marked with * in Table 4; this is what a BAS or remote light sees.

Trip counters: most "opened 3 (default) times" thresholds are set by ECTO parameters (e.g. 1.12/4.14 high pressure, 1.13/4.15 freezestat, 4.04, 3.04, 3.09); a unit configured with a different count will lock out sooner or later than the table states.
The IMC ignores the low-pressure switches during compressor start-up, so a stored low-pressure code (22-29) reflects a real trip after the delay.

Sensor codes 73-78 and 91-99: RT6/RT16/RT17 are 2-wire thermistors, A2 zone sensors are a 2-wire thermistor with a 1k series resistor; measure resistance at the board terminals against the temperature-resistance chart before replacing.

S87 / S88 low pressure switches (shunted by A55 during start-up)
S10 primary limit and rollout switches on gas heat sections

terminalLabels.R: 24 VAC hot to thermostat (Lennox convention - verify on unit controller)
terminalLabels.DO1: Service relay output (closes on selected alarms; Prodigy 2.0/CORE)

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (unit-controller units): on Y1 (or network demand) A55 energizes the indoor blower (B3) and, after proving airflow via S52, energizes compressor contactor K1 (compressor B1) and the condenser fans (B4/B5 via K68); low-pressure switches S87/S88 are shunted during start-up. Y2 brings on the second compressor/stage (B2). High-pressure switch S4/S7 trips de-energize the compressor; three trips = strike-3 lockout (alarm 13).

Heating (gas): on W1 the ignition control A3 checks limits (S10, rollout) and the combustion-air pressure switch, runs the combustion blower prepurge, energizes the spark/igniter and gas valve GV1, and proves flame; the blower starts after the heat-on delay. W2 adds the second heat stage. Repeated ignition failures produce a heat lockout alarm on the unit controller.

Economizer: the unit controller (A55; economizer board A56 EM1 on IMC units) modulates the outdoor-air damper actuator for free cooling when outdoor conditions are suitable; mechanical cooling is staged behind it. The zone sensor A2 supplies the space temperature.
notes: Confirmed against Lennox documents: A55, K1, S4, S87, S88 (wiring diagram 538043-03 and service literature 100087) and B1, B3, B4/B5, K68, T1/CB8, A2, A3, S10, S52, S42, A42 (Unit Information legend 100074). Designators marked 'named in IMC/Prodigy codes' are taken from the alarm texts transcribed in controls[] (manufacturer documents), not from a legend; check every designator against the legend printed on the unit's wiring diagram (inside the control compartment door). Lennox numbering convention: A = controls/boards, B = motors, K = relays/contactors, S = switches, RT = temperature sensors, T = transformers, CB = circuit breakers, GV = gas valves.
The sequence of operation is generic to Lennox unit-controller rooftops; the model-specific sequence is in the unit's service literature ('Unit Information') and IOM.
Landmark/Raider units without a unit controller use conventional 24 V thermostat wiring through relays and a defrost/ignition board.

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor keeps running / will not shut off during high outdoor humidity on a Prodigy 2.0 unit
likelyCauses: BAS/network dehumidification setpoints set unreasonably low by previous technicians, keeping the compressor on (documented resolution in the cited HVAC-Talk thread 2243831; the Lennox-recommended M3 board swap did not fix it)

Dehumidification (Humiditrol / reheat) or humidity-based control parameter keeping mechanical cooling on when the outdoor humidity sensor reads above the setpoint (reported field pattern, forum-level evidence)
Faulty or mis-scaled outdoor/return humidity sensor
checks: Review the BAS/network dehumidification setpoints before replacing the M3 board
Check the humidity sensor readings on the Prodigy display against a calibrated meter
Review dehumidification settings and disable to confirm the behaviour changes
Check Prodigy firmware level and controller parameters against the setup guide
sources: HVAC-Talk thread 'Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Issue' (hvac-talk.com/threads/lennox-prodigy-2-0-issue.2243831/) - resolved by correcting BAS dehumidification setpoints

commonIssues.symptom: Loss of communication between the Prodigy/M2 controller and the network or display; controller replaced more than once
likelyCauses: Controller (Prodigy M2/M3) board failure
Network wiring / termination faults
Poor power quality (erratic power alarms)
checks: Check 24 VAC supply and grounding at A55
Inspect network daisy-chain wiring, polarity and termination
Verify firmware and replace the controller only after wiring and power are proven
sources: HVAC-Talk threads 'Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Issue' and 'Lennox Prodigy Board'

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor locked out on high pressure (IMC code 13 / CORE alarm 13 Strike3 High Press S4)
likelyCauses: Dirty or blocked condenser coil
Outdoor fan motor / capacitor failure
Overcharge or non-condensables
Failed S4 switch
checks: Compare head pressure to outdoor ambient (condenser split) and subcooling
Confirm outdoor fan runs and draws normal amps
Clean coil; check S4 trip/reset points
Clear the lockout from the Service menu (CORE/Prodigy) or reset the IMC after repair
sources: Lennox CORE Application Guide 485115 Table 11 (alarm 13 event action: check charge, fans and coil)

commonIssues.symptom: Nuisance low-pressure trips at compressor start in cold weather
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge or restricted airflow (dirty filters, iced coil) - the A55 controller shunts S87/S88 only during start-up, so trips after the delay are real
Failed low-pressure switch
checks: Verify suction pressure after the start-up shunt period
Check filters, blower operation and evaporator coil
Check S87/S88 continuity and setpoint
sources: Lennox Unit Information service literature 100087 (A55 shunts low pressure switches during start-up)

commonIssues.symptom: Blower alarm / STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER lockout (Prodigy 2.0)
likelyCauses: Broken or slipping blower belt
Blower motor overload or VFD fault
S52 airflow switch or tubing fault
Excessive static (dirty filters, closed dampers)
checks: Inspect belt tension/condition and sheave alignment
Measure blower motor amps vs. FLA; check VFD fault log
Verify S52 switch operation and tubing
Clear the lockout from the UI after repair
sources: Lennox Prodigy 2.0 Application Guide 507242 Table 65 (STRIKE 3 ON BLOWER)

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer not bringing in outdoor air / stuck at minimum or fully open
likelyCauses: Stuck or seized damper / linkage
Failed actuator
Failed or drifted outdoor/return sensors (temperature or enthalpy)
Incorrect changeover settings
checks: Command the damper through the controller's test mode and watch travel
Check actuator power and feedback
Compare sensor readings to a reference thermometer/psychrometer
Review economizer setpoints in the controller
sources: PNNL 'Best Practices for Air-Side Economizers Operation and Maintenance' (stuck dampers, sensor failures, linkages, actuators, settings)
Lennox Economizer for Energence rooftop units instruction (manuals.plus mirror)

notes: Nameplate: the factory MODEL NO. and SERIAL NO. are on the unit rating plate on the compressor/control side; the serial is always 10 characters on 1973+ equipment. Catalog numbers such as L1318 or 45W08 are LennoxPros stock numbers, not model numbers.

Lennox rooftop nomenclature (2009+) is positional: brand letter, unit type (G gas/electric, C electric/electric, H heat pump, D dual fuel), generation/family letter, 3-digit nominal cooling MBH, efficiency (S/H/U), refrigerant (4 = R-410A, 5 = R-454B), blower type, heat input (gas S/M/H, N none), minor design digit, voltage (P 208-230/1, Y 208-230/3, G 460/3, J 575/3), then optional factory-installed option codes.

Family names verified: L Series LGA/LCA/LHA (and LGC/LCC), Strategos SGA/SCA + SGB/SCB + SGC/SCC + SGH/SCH, Energence LGH/LCH, Enlight LGT/LCT/LHT/LDT, Model L LGM/LCM, Xion LGX/LCX/LHX (not XGA/XCA), Landmark KGA/KCA/KHA + KGB/KCB/KHB/KDB, Raider ZGA/ZCA/ZHA + ZGB/ZCB/ZHB + ZGD/ZCD, T-Class TSA/TPA/TAA. Lennox lists Model L, Enlight, Xion and Raider as four distinct lines (comparison sheet 37J72). CBA/CBH/CBX are residential air handlers; 'Elite' ELS/ELC could not be verified.
